$comment: Read by `npm run beta:supply-chain`. Two kinds of exception, both deliberately awkward to add.
`advisories` accepts a NON-blocking production advisory. `high` and `critical` cannot be
accepted here at all — the gate fails on them regardless of what this file says. Every entry
needs an `advisory` (the GHSA id), a `reason` and an `expires`; an expired entry FAILS, so an
acceptance is a decision with a review date rather than a permanent one. An entry for an
advisory the audit no longer reports also fails, because a standing acceptance of a fixed
problem reads as coverage.
`advisory` is required and is checked against the GHSA the audit actually reports. It was added
on 2026-09-11 after the quill entry was found accepting `GHSA-4943-9vgg-gr5r`, a 2021 advisory
affecting quill <= 1.3.7, while 2.0.3 was installed — so the advisory that really applied had
never been reviewed, and this gate called the acceptance satisfied on every run because the
package NAME matched. Keying on the name accepts a package; keying on the id accepts a finding.
`affects` is optional, and when present must equal the audit's reported range, so an upgrade
into a newly-affected range cannot pass under a review of the old one.
`mitigations` is where the source pointers go, and it is machine-checked. Each entry names a
`file`, a `declaration` (the literal declaration text, which must be UNIQUE in that file), a
`claim`, and optionally a `guard` that must appear inside that declaration's body. It was added
on 2026-09-21, after four of the quill entry's five reviews had each found at least one stale
source pointer. Line numbers are the part that rots: they shift when anyone inserts a method
above them and nothing complains. Declaration text does not.
A `guard` must be EXECUTABLE CODE. The file is parsed and the body is matched with comments and
string/template literals blanked, so `expect(x).not.toContain(` works as a guard and `'<script'`
does not. That is deliberate: the first version of the check used raw text, and commenting out
`DOMPurify.sanitize(...)` left it green because the string was still there, in a comment.
Anchors are matched with only comments blanked, so a test name inside a string literal can still
be anchored on while a declaration quoted in a doc comment cannot.
Like `affects`, the field is optional, since an acceptance can rest on something with no code to
point at; but when present it is fully verified, and a present-but-empty array fails. It does
NOT check that the claim is true — only that the code the claim names still exists and still
contains the guard.
`unreferencedDependencies` excuses a production dependency that no source file imports. Four
of these turned out to be genuinely unused — `openai`, `express`, `cors`, `dotenv` — and were
removed rather than listed. An entry here means the package is required by something other
than an import: the Angular runtime, a version pin, or the ng-mocks stub. The pins and the stub
listed today are left over from ADF, which left the tree in NXSAT-637; NXSAT-672 removes them.
If the package becomes referenced, or stops being a dependency, its entry fails as unnecessary.

quill.reason: GHSA-v3m3-f69x-jf25 — XSS via Quill's HTML export, affecting quill = 2.0.3, which is what we run and is the latest published release. Verified against the registry on 2026-09-21: 2.0.3 is still the `latest` dist-tag, nothing newer than it has ever been published, and the advisory still records `first_patched_version: null`. There is nothing to upgrade to, so this cannot be closed by a version bump. Not reachable as configured, on both directions of travel; the source pointers for every claim below now live in `mitigations` and are checked by the supply-chain gate rather than asserted in prose. WRITE: readQuillHtml() passes getSemanticHTML() through DOMPurify.sanitize() before returning, and that return value is what onSave() emits and the parent persists. getSemanticHTML()'s only other caller, applyExternalContent(), compares the value for equality and discards it. READ: a text/html note is rendered by the htmlReadonlyView computed, which passes the stored content through renderTrustedHtml() — that is the path a Quill-authored note actually takes back to a reader, and it is row 4 of the Category D table in docs/sonarcloud-security-remediation-plan.md. Each half is enforced by a different thing, and neither covers the other: the READ path by sanitizer-audit.mjs check 5, which walks the AST to require a sanitise call paired with every bypassSecurityTrustHtml; the WRITE path by the note-editor.spec.ts test named in mitigations[3], which drives onSave() with hostile markup and asserts what saveNote emits. sanitizer-audit check 5 CANNOT cover the exporter — it fires on the presence of bypassSecurityTrustHtml and readQuillHtml() has none, it returns a plain string — so before that test existed, deleting the sanitise call left every gate green while raw Quill output was persisted. Revisit on the next Quill release or when the editor is replaced.

mitigations.claim: WRITE path. The only place Quill's vulnerable getSemanticHTML() export reaches the server: its output is sanitised here before onSave() emits it and the parent persists it.

mitigations.declaration: private applyExternalContent(html: string, force = false): void
mitigations.claim: The only other caller of getSemanticHTML(). It compares the export for equality and discards it, so the unsanitised value never escapes this method.
READ path. The route a stored text/html note takes back to a reader, sanitised via renderTrustedHtml(). Enforced independently by sanitizer-audit.mjs check 5.

$corrections: Re-reviewed 2026-09-11 because the previous entry was wrong in every verifiable particular while its conclusion was right — the most believable kind of stale acceptance, and one this gate cannot catch, since it matches entries by package name and never reads the GHSA or the line numbers.

It cited GHSA-4943-9vgg-gr5r, a 2021 advisory affecting quill <= 1.3.7. We run 2.0.3, so that advisory does not apply to this repository at all, and the advisory that does — GHSA-v3m3-f69x-jf25, published 2026-01-13 — was therefore accepted by accident rather than by decision.
All four source pointers were stale: document-detail.ts:1694 and :3133 are an unrelated collection check and a lock comment; note-editor.ts:89 and :95 are an imageUploading signal and an editor ref.

It named the guardrail `checkSanitizerPairing`. That was not a false claim when written, but it is now: the check was deliberately removed and superseded by sanitizer-audit.mjs check 5, which is AST-based rather than regex-based. The protection is real and stronger; only the name was wrong.

Second review pass, same day: the correction above then overstated things in its own turn, by naming check 5 as the enforcement for ALL of it. Review caught that check 5 cannot see the exporter at all, since it triggers on bypassSecurityTrustHtml and readQuillHtml() contains none. The mitigation this whole acceptance rests on had no enforcement of any kind. A test was added and confirmed to fail when the sanitise call is removed. Recorded because the failure repeated inside one file in one day: a claim about which gate covers a mitigation is as easy to get wrong as the mitigation itself, and nothing machine-checks it.

Fifth review, 2026-09-21, prompted by asking whether Dependabot #106 should be fixed or dismissed. Conclusion unchanged and every substantive claim re-verified first-hand: quill 2.0.3 is still the latest published release, so there is nothing to fix; the WRITE, READ and discard paths all still hold; and the regression test still asserts both that hostile markup is stripped AND that legitimate content survives, so a sanitiser returning '' could not pass it. Dismissing the GitHub alert was rejected as strictly weaker than this entry: a dismissal has no expiry, npm audit ignores it so this entry would still be required, and the only honest GitHub reason — 'vulnerable code not used' — is false, since getSemanticHTML() IS called on two paths and is mitigated downstream rather than unused.

The fifth review first reported that three of the four line numbers had gone stale again, and that was WRONG — the fifth wrong pointer claim in this entry's history, this time made by the reviewer rather than found by one. On main, 502-503 are exactly the getSemanticHTML()/DOMPurify.sanitize pair, 484-485 the equality compare, 118-120 the renderTrustedHtml call; every number was correct. The reading came from a working tree checked out on an unrelated feature branch with uncommitted edits to note-editor.ts, which shifted the file by about 23 lines. Caught by Copilot on the pull request, which compared the claim against main. Recorded rather than quietly deleted, because the error is the argument: a pointer claim in this entry has now been got wrong five times by five different readers, one of whom was checking specifically for that failure and still read the wrong tree.

That is why the pointers were still moved into `mitigations`: not because they were stale this time, but because whether they are stale is a question nobody reliably answers by hand. Anchors are declaration text rather than line numbers, and uniqueness per file is load-bearing — a bare `readQuillHtml` matches three times in note-editor.ts, twice as a call, so anchoring on the first would resolve the wrong function's body entirely.

The check itself shipped with two holes, both found in review and both demonstrated before fixing. It matched raw text, so commenting out `DOMPurify.sanitize(...)` left it GREEN — the exact regression it exists to catch — and a `{` inside a string literal would unbalance its brace counter and run the 'body' past the end of the function. It now parses the file, takes the body from the AST, and blanks comments and literals before matching the guard. A gate that could be satisfied by its own subject's comments is worse than no gate, because it reports coverage.

Third review pass, same day: the READ path was cited as document-detail.ts:1862 and :3394. Both sit inside `if (mime === 'text/markdown')` branches, so neither renders the text/html content Quill's export produces — the pointers named real sanitised code that is irrelevant to this advisory. The actual path is note-editor.ts:118-120. That is the FOURTH stale or wrong source pointer found in this one entry, across three reviews in a single day, and the pattern is now the point: the prose in this field carries the whole argument and nothing verifies a word of it. The `advisory` and `affects` fields were added precisely to move some of that burden onto the gate; the source pointers remain unverified by anything but a reader.

unreferencedDependencies.tslib: Emitted helper library. The TypeScript compiler generates imports of it into the build output; no source file names it.
unreferencedDependencies.@angular/animations: Required by @angular/material at runtime for its transitions. Never imported by our source.
unreferencedDependencies.@mat-datetimepicker/core: Version pin left over from ADF: an @alfresco/adf-core peer, and one of the two pins that deliberately differed from adf-core's suggestion, because its major track is offset from Angular's (16.0.1 for Angular 20). adf-core left the tree in NXSAT-637 and no package depends on this one now; NXSAT-672 drops it.
unreferencedDependencies.pdfjs-dist: Version pin left over from ADF: an @alfresco/adf-core peer, and the second deliberate deviation, because 4.x downgrades a shared native package (6.2.108). adf-core left the tree in NXSAT-637 and no package depends on this one now; NXSAT-672 drops it.
unreferencedDependencies.minimatch: Version pin left over from ADF: @alfresco/adf-core declared it as a `>=10.0.0` peer. adf-core left the tree in NXSAT-637, but the pin still decides the copy hoisted to the root, which the dev tooling asking for `^10` resolves to (@typescript-eslint/typescript-estree, test-exclude and ignore-walk among them), so NXSAT-672 re-decides it rather than just deleting it.
unreferencedDependencies.angular-oauth2-oidc: Version pin left over from ADF: a direct dependency of @alfresco/adf-core, pinned so a clean install could not float it. adf-core left the tree in NXSAT-637 and no package depends on this one now; NXSAT-672 drops it.
unreferencedDependencies.ng-mocks: Not a library: `file:tools/stubs/ng-mocks`, a stub that stood in for the real test-mocking package because @alfresco/adf-hx-content-services imported `ngMocks` from its shipped /ui bundle (see scripts/beta-harness/no-test-libs-in-bundle.mjs). Our source never imports it. adf-hx left the tree in NXSAT-637; the stub and this entry go in NXSAT-672.
